moments: Prologue: during the Vs. Tour, Pearl Jam refused to play Los Angeles because of their dispute with Ticketmaster over service charges. They played the Empire Polo Club in Indio instead, for almost 25,000 people.
Paul Tollett, whose Goldenvoice booked the date, has said this show planted the seed for the festival.
firsts: First large concert at the Empire Polo Club

sources.publication: Los Angeles Times (Steve Hochman, 'Pearl Jam Blossoms in Desert', p. F3), via Wikipedia 'Coachella' footnote

notes: Not a Coachella edition. The LA Times original was not fetched; the attendance figure is from its Wikipedia citation.

attendance: roughly 17,000-20,000 per day (Ringer); Wikipedia: ~17,000 day one + ~20,000 day two = ~37,000
capacity: Goldenvoice hoped for roughly double the actual turnout (Ringer: 'about half of what Goldenvoice had hoped')
gross: Not reported. Tollett put the loss at 'around a million dollars' (Ringer); GRAMMY.com gives $850,000
moments: Ran in October heat over 100 degrees. Kid Koala said his vinyl melted mid-set.
Lost money badly. Tom Morello says the festival asked Rage for its fee back; Far Out reports they returned half.
Undercard included the Chemical Brothers, Moby, Morrissey, Underworld, DJ Shadow, A Perfect Circle and Jurassic 5. Ninja Tune supplied nine acts.
firsts: First Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival
Empire Polo Club as the festival site
notes: Wikipedia says Pollstar named it festival of the year; not independently verified.

moments: Skipped after the 1999 losses. Per Wikipedia, Tollett blamed oversaturation of Southern California festivals.
Goldenvoice instead co-staged Pasquale Rotella's Nocturnal Wonderland at the Empire Polo Club in September 2000.
notes: The oversaturation reason and the Nocturnal Wonderland swap come only from Wikipedia. The Ringer says only that the loss meant it 'did not return in 2000 at all'.

moments: Moved to spring and cut to one day. Jane's Addiction headlined, with Perry Farrell in a white jumpsuit and fedora.

Rest of the bill: Weezer, The Roots, Mos Def, Fatboy Slim (closing with a 90-minute set), Paul Oakenfold, the Chemical Brothers (who covered 'Iron Man'), and Sigur Ros (their first Southern California show).
In March 2001 Tollett agreed to sell Goldenvoice to AEG, reportedly for $7 million.
firsts: First edition under AEG ownership of Goldenvoice
notes: The $65 price and the $7M AEG sale figure come via Wikipedia footnotes.

headliners: Siouxsie and the Banshees (reunion, per Wikipedia)
moments: Bjork drew one of the day's biggest crowds and came back for the encore wearing a large green shell on her dress.
The Chemical Brothers closed Saturday, and Oasis played Sunday.
The Sahara tent already had a laser show projected onto circular screens.
firsts: Queens of the Stone Age called the first local Coachella Valley band to play (Wikipedia)
notes: Attendance and the Siouxsie reunion billing are from Wikipedia only. The Daily Bruin confirms a Sahara tent with lasers by 2002, so the Sahara is not a later addition.

attendance: around 30,000 per day (Las Vegas Sun); Wikipedia gives 60,000 total
moments: Iggy Pop reunited with Ron and Scott Asheton as the Stooges, their first show together in about 30 years. The Las Vegas Sun ranked it second-best of the weekend.
MCA gave an anti-war speech during the Beastie Boys' set, weeks after the invasion of Iraq, and the crowd reaction was mixed.
The White Stripes and Blur also played the main stage. Co-founder Rick Van Santen died that December, aged 41.
firsts: First on-site camping (Wikipedia: 2,252 sites; OC Weekly calls 2004 'the second year camping was permitted')

sources.publication: OC Weekly (Mary Carreon), 'The Evolution of Coachella's Campgrounds'

notes: The Las Vegas Sun page header shows a 2024 date, but the URL path is 2003/may/02. The 2,252 campsite count is Wikipedia-only.

attendance: roughly 100,000 over two days, about 50,000 per day (Las Vegas Sun); Wikipedia gives 110,000
ga_price: $75 per day or $142 for both days
moments: The Pixies' reunion was one of the biggest stories of the weekend. Beck and the Flaming Lips also played.
Radiohead headlined despite fears they would cancel, but booming bass from the second stage bled into their quieter songs.
Temperatures went above 100 degrees, and Saturday afternoon was described as brutal.

sources.publication: Rolling Stone, 'Flashback: The Pixies Reunite at Coachella in 2004'

notes: The Pixies were billed below the two headliners, not as a headliner. AEG bought half of Coachella in 2004 (Ringer). Wikipedia says Tollett regrets not adding a third day for Bowie; unverified.

headliners: New Order (Sunday closer after NIN, per Rolling Stone)
attendance: about 50,000 per day expected (Las Vegas Sun); Rolling Stone estimated 50,000
capacity: not sold out at press time (Las Vegas Sun, Apr 29)
ga_price: $81 per day or $152 for two days
moments: Arcade Fire played Sunday on the Outdoor Stage. Rolling Stone called the set 'galvanizing' and said it drew a massive crowd.
Bauhaus reunited for the first time since 1998, with Peter Murphy hanging upside down during 'Bela Lugosi's Dead'. Gang of Four's original lineup played its first North American show since 1981.
Coldplay's 'Yellow' turned into a crowd singalong.
notes: The lineup had 92 acts on five stages. Wikipedia says a Cocteau Twins reunion was cancelled; not checked.

attendance: more than 100,000 over two days (Billboard); Wikipedia gives 120,000
moments: Daft Punk debuted the LED pyramid in the Sahara tent on Saturday night. Water & Music describes a tent built for about 10,000 that reportedly held more than 40,000, and says the show set off a live-production 'arms race'.
Madonna played the Sahara dance tent, came on about 20 minutes late to boos, and did about six songs. Billboard called it a fun novelty but a logistical nightmare.
Kanye West, Massive Attack (with Liz Fraser), Gnarls Barkley and Scissor Sisters were also on the bill.

sources.publication: Billboard (Jonathan Cohen, Todd Martens, Brian Cohen reporting)

notes: Ticket price not verified. The 40,000-in-the-tent figure is reported, not documented.

attendance: 186,000-187,000 aggregate (Wikipedia); Billboard via Dancing Astronaut gives '62,000 attendees', likely a daily figure
moments: Rage Against the Machine closed Sunday, Apr 29, their first show since splitting in 2000. They opened with 'Testify', and Zack de la Rocha made a political statement during 'Wake Up'.
OC Weekly reports a riot in the campground after the Rage set, with helicopters and SWAT present. Diffuser reports fires and damaged art installations.
firsts: Stagecoach country festival launched on the same grounds (May 2007)

moments: Prince headlined Saturday, played past midnight and declared 'From now on, this is Prince's house!' His cover of Radiohead's 'Creep' became the story of the weekend. His team had the fan footage taken down, and he restored it himself in 2015.
Roger Waters played Dark Side of the Moon. The inflatable pig was let go and floated off into the night.
notes: Wikipedia says 2008 lost money because of unsold tickets and high booking fees; not checked against a primary source. Prince's reported fee ($4-5M in listicles) is unverified.

ga_price: $269 three-day (layaway plan offered); $120 single day at the door
moments: Paul McCartney opened the festival on Friday with a two-and-a-half-hour set and two encores. Wikipedia says he ran 54 minutes past curfew.
The Cure's set was cut off after running about 30 minutes past curfew. Leonard Cohen made a rare appearance.
firsts: First layaway payment plan for passes (per AP description)

sources.publication: Associated Press, via The Washington Times

notes: The curfew overrun figures are from Wikipedia. It is not confirmed that layaway was a first; the AP only says it was offered.

capacity: all 75,000 three-day passes sold out in advance (BizBash)
moments: Overcrowding: LA Weekly reported gate-crashing, fistfights and 'near-riot' conditions at the gates on Friday, counterfeit tickets, three-hour entry waits, and a near-crush at an exit on Sunday. Tollett said in 2011: 'The mistakes were in the planning.'
The Eyjafjallajokull volcanic ash cloud stranded seven acts in England.
Jay-Z brought out Beyonce as a surprise guest.
firsts: First year selling three-day passes only, on nontransferable wristbands (BizBash)
Ferris wheel on site by this year (BizBash)
Webcast of individual sets (CBS/CNET; the full YouTube multistage stream came in 2011)

sources.publication: Las Vegas Sun, 'After rough 2010, Coachella tries to iron itself out'

notes: 'The crush' was overcrowding and gate-crashing. No mass-casualty crowd crush was reported. UPI counted 69 arrests over the weekend.

attendance: 225,000 aggregate, 75,000 paid per day (Wikipedia); Tollett would not announce capacity in advance
ga_price: $269 three-day plus fees (resale at $400 and up)
moments: Fixes after 2010: a wrought-iron perimeter fence, an extra road lane partly funded by Goldenvoice, and an end to the ticket-for-wristband exchange.
YouTube streamed three stages on separate channels, about 61 bands with Wrigley as sponsor, and nearly 4 million people watched.
On May 31, 2011, Goldenvoice announced a second identical weekend for 2012.
notes: The Strokes were also top-billed. Wikipedia lists 'Kanye West / The Strokes'.

attendance: 158,387 paid across both weekends (80,726 + 77,661) (Wikipedia, Billboard Boxscore footnote)
capacity: W1 sold out in about 40 minutes, W2 about two hours later (mxdwn)
moments: The Tupac 'hologram' during Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg's set on Apr 15: a Pepper's ghost projection on Mylar. Digital Domain built it, AV Concepts staged it, and it was Dre's idea.
First year with two weekends. Tollett preferred cloning the festival to adding about 40,000 people a day.
notes: This corrects an implied $315 GA (from Wikipedia's '$349, up $34'): the advertised 2012 price was $285 plus fees. Dancing Astronaut notes that 2013 prices no longer carried the extra service charges, which may explain the gap. The 2012 gross was not seen directly in a Billboard source.

moments: Poetic Kinetics' giant snail installation (Wikipedia).
Indio approved a deal keeping the festival there through 2030 and raising the city's per-ticket fee from $2.33 to $5.01 starting in 2014.
notes: No single defining moment was verified in this pass.

attendance: 96,500 per day, 579,000 admissions across six days (Billboard via SPIN)
vip_price: Wikipedia: VIP over $5,000 (likely a premium package, not standard VIP)
gross: $78,332,000 (Billboard via SPIN / Dancing Astronaut), the third straight record year
moments: Outkast reunited for their first shows in about a decade, with Janelle Monae and Future as guests. It was the festival's most-tweeted moment, and Billboard called it 'imperfect'.
AXS TV broadcast weekend two (Wikipedia). Heineken House debuted.
firsts: TV broadcast of weekend 2 on AXS TV (Wikipedia)
notes: Wikipedia calls the 579,000 figure a typo. It is not: it is cumulative daily admissions (96,500 x 6). Unique attendees would be about 193,000.

moments: On weekend one Sunday, Madonna appeared during Drake's set and kissed him. His visible reaction went viral.
AC/DC headlined Friday despite online grumbling, and LAist said the whole crowd sang along.

sources.publication: Pollstar 2015 Year End Top 20 Worldwide Festival Grosses (PDF mirror)

notes: The PDF is a third-party mirror of the Pollstar chart.

capacity: 100% sold. In March 2016 Indio raised the daily cap from 99,000 to 125,000, effective the following year (Wikipedia)
gross: $94,218,000 (Pollstar 2016 year-end; the chart misprints it as '$94,218,0000')
moments: Guns N' Roses with Slash and Duff McKagan: Axl Rose had broken his foot and performed seated on a guitar-studded throne built by Dave Grohl. He brought out Angus Young the day his move to AC/DC as frontman was announced.
Weekend two included tributes to Prince, who died Apr 21, 2016 (Wikipedia).
firsts: Same year Goldenvoice staged Desert Trip on the grounds in October ($160.1M gross)

sources.publication: Pollstar 2016 Year End Top 20 Worldwide Festival Grosses (PDF)

notes: Wikipedia also lists an N.W.A reunion with Ice Cube on weekend one; not verified here.

gross: $114,593,000 (Pollstar). The first recurring festival to gross over $100M (Billboard via Dancing Astronaut)
moments: Beyonce withdrew on doctors' advice during her pregnancy, and Lady Gaga took the Saturday slot.
Radiohead's Friday weekend-one set lost sound at least four times, starting during 'Ful Stop'. Thom Yorke joked about aliens.
Tollett told The New Yorker each headliner was paid $3-4M.
firsts: La Grande XL Ferris wheel debuted, replacing the original La Grande wheel (LA Times)

sources.publication: Pollstar 2017 Year End Top 20 Worldwide Festival Grosses (PDF)
Los Angeles Times (Vanessa Franko), via TNS / Brunswick News
mxdwn (McKenzie Dillon), relaying The New Yorker

notes: Scenes for A Star Is Born were filmed here (Wikipedia; unverified). The Anschutz anti-LGBTQ donations controversy broke in Jan 2017 (The FADER, 2017-01-05).

moments: Beychella: Beyonce headlined Saturday, Apr 14 and Apr 21, the first Black woman to headline. The two-hour HBCU-homecoming show had a drumline and marching band, a Destiny's Child reunion, Jay-Z, and Solange. Netflix released Homecoming on Apr 17, 2019.
40 mph winds kept the weekend-two campgrounds closed until 3 a.m. Friday, and many campers waited in a Walmart parking lot (OC Weekly).
notes: GRAMMY.com gives 'April 13 and 22', which is wrong: she played the Saturday slots, Apr 14 and Apr 21. Wikipedia reports booking fees around $8M and Teen Vogue harassment reporting; not verified.

moments: Ariana Grande, at 25, was the youngest headliner and the fourth woman to headline. She reunited four members of NSYNC (not Justin Timberlake), and Diddy, Mase and Nicki Minaj also came out.
Kanye West was ruled out as a headliner after demanding a custom dome stage (The Guardian, Jan 14, 2019). He held his first public Sunday Service on Easter, Apr 21, in the campgrounds instead.
Lead rigger Christopher Griffin, 49, died in a fall during setup on Apr 6. Solange cancelled a week before.
firsts: Both weekends livestreamed on YouTube for the first time (USA Today, 2019-04-08)

sources.publication: AFP (Maggy Donaldson), via The Jakarta Post
Wikipedia 'Coachella 2019' (citing The Guardian 2019-01-14, NME 2019-04-01, Desert Sun 2019-04-08, USA Today 2019-04-08)

notes: GA sold out in about 40 minutes and all passes in six hours (IQ). Justin Bieber guested with Ariana on weekend two (widely reported; not fetched).

dates: Cancelled (scheduled Apr 10-12 and Apr 17-19; moved to Oct 9-11 and 16-18, then cancelled)
moments: Postponed to October in March 2020 over COVID-19. Riverside County health officer Dr. Cameron Kaiser cancelled it in June 2020.
The documentary '20 Years in the Desert' premiered on YouTube on Apr 10, 2020.

sources.publication: CNN (Chloe Melas, Sandra Gonzalez), via Wikipedia
Pollstar, 'Coachella Releasing Free Documentary On YouTube'

notes: The exact October dates were not verified.

moments: Cancelled again under California pandemic restrictions. Riverside County's health officer formally cancelled it in January 2021.
Oct 2021: Goldenvoice signed a new Empire Polo Club lease running to 2050.
notes: Find a primary (Desert Sun or LA Times) source for the January 2021 cancellation.

headliners: Swedish House Mafia and The Weeknd (replacing Ye)
attendance: not reported. Variety reported that Styles' opening-night crowd topped 100,000
moments: Ye dropped out about Apr 4, less than two weeks before. Swedish House Mafia and The Weeknd were announced as replacements on Apr 6.
Harry Styles brought out Shania Twain on weekend one and Lizzo on weekend two.

First edition after the pandemic. Rage Against the Machine and Travis Scott (removed after Astroworld) were carried over from 2020 and didn't play. 2NE1 reunited, and Brockhampton played their final shows.
firsts: 88rising's 'Head in the Clouds' showcase as the first full-label showcase (Rank Magazine, via Wikipedia)

sources.publication: Variety, 'Harry Styles' Coachella Crowd Topped 100,000' (via Wikipedia)

notes: Billie Eilish (20) would beat Ariana (25) as youngest headliner, but no source confirming the claim was found. Check before publishing.

capacity: weekend 2 did not sell out, the first time since 2012 (Desert Sun)
moments: Bad Bunny opened Friday as the first Latin, Spanish-language headliner. Post Malone joined for 'La Cancion'.
BLACKPINK became the first Korean or Asian act to headline. All three headliners were nonwhite, a first.

Frank Ocean started about an hour late after a planned ice-rink show was scrapped, following leg fractures from an on-site injury. He pulled out of weekend two and Blink-182 replaced him. Goldenvoice was fined $133,000 for curfew overruns.
firsts: All six stages livestreamed (TechCrunch 2023-04-03, not fetched)
notes: Wikipedia cites Billboard (2023-04-21) for losses of 'millions' and over $4M on the unused rink. The $4M figure was not seen directly.

moments: The slowest sales in a decade: weekend one took 27 days to sell out, and sales were down 14-17% year over year.
No Doubt played their first show since 2015, with Olivia Rodrigo as a guest.
Billie Eilish joined Lana Del Rey for 'Ocean Eyes' and 'Video Games'.
notes: Stagecoach 2024 (89,003) outsold each Coachella weekend. The KESQ counts (about 81K per weekend) are far below the 125K daily cap; these may be city-taxed tickets only.

attendance: about 120,000 per weekend, about 240,000 total (NBC Palm Springs); Wikipedia gives about 245,000
capacity: W1 GA sold out by Dec 2024; W2 widely available, resold below face by April
ga_price: $549 at Dec 2024 tier; $649 W1 / $599 W2 by April 2025
moments: Lady Gaga debuted the Mayhem show ('Mayhem in the Desert'), an opera-house set in four acts. She was the second woman to headline twice, after Bjork.
Green Day's Coachella debut included a 'not part of the MAGA agenda' line. Travis Scott built 'The Village by Cactus Jack'.
The LA Philharmonic, conducted by Gustavo Dudamel, became the first major orchestra to play (Apr 12).
firsts: YouTube dedicated Coachella livestream app (Sherwood News)
notes: The Go-Go's played their first show since 2022. Charli XCX brought out Lorde, Billie Eilish and Troye Sivan.

capacity: GA and VIP for both weekends sold out within about three days of the Sep 2025 on-sale (VICE; Rolling Stone 2025-09-22)
gross: not reported (Latin Post's $220-240M claim is unsourced; do not use)
moments: Justin Bieber's first headline set was reportedly paid 'north of $10 million' (Rolling Stone, via Complex). He played a laptop/YouTube nostalgia segment and a stripped-down B-stage set from Swag, with guests including SZA and Billie Eilish on weekend two.
Karol G became the first Latina headliner. Madonna joined Sabrina Carpenter on weekend two for the live debut of 'Bring Your Love'.

The 'bunker': Radiohead's KID A MNESIA Motion Picture House, a roughly 17,000 sq ft underground installation without the band. Wind cancelled Anyma's weekend-one set, and the Strokes closed Apr 18 with visuals condemning strikes on Iran and Gaza.
firsts: Permanent-construction underground art venue on the grounds

sources.publication: Complex (Trace William Cowen), relaying Rolling Stone

notes: This was the 25th edition. The lineup was announced unusually early, on Sep 15, 2025. In Sep 2026 YouTube extended its livestream deal through 2030, and says the 2026 stream set a concurrent-viewer record but gave no number.
